subject: AtlasPay: performance gating + pilot plan to choose Hosted vs Dedicated
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Apr 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: AtlasPay: performance gating + pilot plan to choose Hosted vs Dedicated

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum while your infra team validates requirements. I kept this focused on the deployment decision (Hosted API vs Dedicated) based on the latency/throughput signals you shared.

Recap from your side:
- Primary product: real-time payment risk scoring on checkout (sub-100ms perceived latency target from frontend).
- Current signal: ~800 reqs/sec peak on evenings, sustained 250–350 qps; bursts to 1.5k qps during promos.
- Model: ~1.2B decoder model, avg output length small (token cost low), but KV cache contributes to memory pressure on long-lived sessions.
- Data sensitivity: no PII in inference payloads; full transaction logs stored in your internal DB.

Key question we agreed to answer in the pilot:
1) Can Hosted API meet your 95th percentile latency target (<120ms end-to-end) for the steady state and during bursts?
2) If not, what Dedicated capacity size and latency SLOs do we need (GPUs / reserved slots) to guarantee SLOs and cost envelope?

Proposed pilot (actionable items):
- Redwood runs a 2-week performance pilot against a controlled traffic replay you provide (we recommend 72 hours of production-like traffic for initial pass).
- Phase A (Hosted): run replay against Redwood Hosted with binning of request sizes and TTL to exercise KV cache. Measure p95, p99, cold-start rates, and cost per 1M tokens.
- Phase B (Dedicated — warm nodes): run same replay on a Dedicated pool sized per our initial estimate (we'll include a 20% buffer). Compare latency curves and the cost delta.
- Deliverables: quantitative p50/p95/p99, tail-CPU/GPU metrics, model memory hit rates, and a recommendation matrix.

Next steps I need from AtlasPay this week:
- A sanitized 72-hour traffic replay (or representative traffic generator config) and QPS profile (Rajesh).
- Confirmation whether you require VPC-only traffic for the pilot (you mentioned gating on procurement).
- Any procurement constraints that would block Dedicated (terms, timeline).

I've attached a one-page pilot scope and a latency/throughput matrix to help your infra team. Ben and Grace are looped for technical sizing and SRE-level runbook.

If this plan looks good, can we target a kick-off on Monday 4/24?

Cheers,

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- atlaspay-pilot-scope-v1.pdf (1 page)
- latency-throughput-matrix.xlsx (workbook, sheet: traffic-bins)
From: Elena Soto <elena@atlaspay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Menon <rajesh.m@atlaspay.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasPay: performance gating + pilot plan to choose Hosted vs Dedicated

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Rajesh and I reviewed internally; a few clarifications and constraints from our infra team:

1) We can produce a sanitized 72-hour replay by tomorrow. It will include the promo bursts (~1.5k qps).
2) For the pilot, we prefer traffic to route from our US east region (us-east-1).
3) Important: Procurement will only sign a Dedicated contract if there's a clear cost delta and an SLA improvement. Otherwise we prefer Hosted for time-to-market.
4) We cannot share raw payloads externally; will provide sanitized inputs with the same QPS/size distribution.

Two technical asks for Redwood before kick-off:
- Can you include a test that mimics the client-side perceived latency (frontend → Redwood → model → backend) so we capture network hops?
- Please include p99 measurements but also breakdown of token generation vs overhead.

We are fine to kick off Monday 4/24. Please send a calendar invite with the pilot runbook and an expected timeline.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Soto | Head of Platform | AtlasPay
elena@atlaspay.com | +1 (617) 555-4433
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@atlaspay.com>, Rajesh Menon <rajesh.m@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 07:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: AtlasPay: performance gating + pilot plan to choose Hosted vs Dedicated

Elena / Rajesh — quick technical note before we run the replay:

- We'll provision a Hosted test harness in us-east-1 and instrument synthetic clients to simulate frontend TCP/TLS latency. That will give you an end-to-end perceived latency baseline (we'll capture client→edge→model→backend traces).
- For Dedicated sizing, initial estimate: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool) to meet <120ms p95 at 1.5k qps with caching. We'll validate during Phase B and revise.
- Cost callout: our initial modeling shows Hosted may meet steady-state but could show higher p99 during burst windows; Dedicated smooths tails but has a higher baseline monthly commit. We'll deliver a side-by-side TCO for your finance team.

Small ask — can Rajesh share any existing latency SLOs (frontend p95/p99) you have? That helps us map measurements to your user impact.

I'll attach the runbook link to the calendar invite.

-b
Ben Carter | Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment referenced: test-runbook (link included in calendar invite)

Subject: RE: AtlasPay: performance gating + pilot plan to choose Hosted vs Dedicated

Thanks everyone — calendar invite sent for Monday 4/24 10:00 AM ET with a short pre-kickoff (30m) and then the test window schedule. Links are in the invite (HubSpot deal + Drive folder).

Action items captured (owners):
- AtlasPay: provide sanitized 72-hour replay + latency SLOs (Rajesh) — ETA: 4/24 EOD.
- Redwood (Ben): provision Hosted harness in us-east-1 and prepare Dedicated pool baseline.
- Redwood (Grace): prepare measurement dashboard (p50/p95/p99, token vs overhead, cost estimates).
- Redwood (Marissa): finalize pilot terms and upload pilot scope to Drive (attached).

If procurement flags prevent Dedicated commitment, we will still run Phase B on a time-limited Dedicated pool for the purpose of measurement only (no long-term financial commitment) — that was the fallback we discussed on the call.

Look forward to the kick-off.

—Marissa
